The problem · Das Problem
The pest rides the crop rotation.
Die Zikade reist mit der Fruchtfolge.
1
Sugar beet. Adults feed on it and spread SBR and Stolbur.
2
Wheat sown right after beet. The nymphs overwinter in it – the nursery.
3
June flight. Adults fly to the nearest beet. The loop closes.
Break step 2 and up to 90 % fewer nymphs survive (LIZ); about 80 % fewer adults (LLG).
Sources: LIZ, JKI 2025, LLG 2026 · typical Kraichgau rotation: sugar beet → winter wheat → winter barley

metres from the beet parcel to the nearest nursery
≈ 350 m
best-fit flight distance (band 250–500 m), from a decay fit on every beet parcel. The literature had no number.
So the neighbourhood is small. The planner now uses 0.5 km, not 1 km – and the advice is concrete: talk to the neighbour whose wheat touches your beet.
And choosing pays. The right fifth of the nurseries removes 37 % of the pressure on the region’s beet. Any fifth: about 20 %.
Same caveat: an exposure–symptom association, not a measured infection · fit Δ ~ e^(−d ⁄ r), r profiled 50 m – 3 km · NASA HLS S30

What we built · live at crop-circles.streamlit.app
Six pages, one decision – for farmer, advisor and office.
My field
Four risks in plain words: planthopper, soil washing away, dry summers, heat. This season seen from space. Prints as one page.
What to grow
Rotations ranked live by your priorities: soil, water, nitrogen, planthopper, income, rotation rules.
Plan 2026–2030
Cut and merge your plots on the map, paint crops, see rule breaks in red, compare with the best match and neighbours’ shared plans.
Our region
Every parcel since 2018: who spreads the planthopper, who receives it. The right fifth of nurseries removes 37 % of the pressure.
Neighbours
One feed for notes, questions and alerts to the plant-protection office, with the field’s figures attached. Roles: farmer, advisor, office.
How we know
18 public datasets, 7 from NASA: HLS, MODIS, SMAP, GPM IMERG, POWER, NASADEM, ECOSTRESS. Method, glossary and every licence.
English and Deutsch · on the phone · optional “Ask about this field”: a language model explains only the page’s numbers
